exposure: neuraxial morphine injection (intrathecal or epidural spaces)
outcome: postoperative overt urinary retention necessitating bladder catheterization
repeat doses of postoperative anesthesia (oral analgesia, intravenous analgesia, oral opioids, intravenous opioids)
cohort: The study included patients undergoing Cesarean deliveries, comparing those who received neuraxial morphine to a historical cohort who did not.
finding: Neuraxial morphine administered during Cesarean delivery significantly increased the rate of postoperative urinary retention (5% vs. 1%, P=0.003) but reduced the need for repeat doses of postoperative analgesia.
mod_finding: Neuraxial morphine used during Cesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk of postoperative urinary retention.
followup_time: Acute postoperative period for urinary retention and analgesia needs, and 30 days for readmission.
